batchId: Claude manual-research batch mcu-01 (7 MCU identities from the Needs manual research list)
method: Web search snippets from the cited pages; claims the snippet did not support were left out or listed under unknowns. No numeric tiers or win probabilities. All records stay provisional until a different contributor checks the cited support.
baselineContinuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe unless a record says otherwise.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Drax the Destroyer (Dave Bautista), Guardians of the Galaxy films through Endgame. Excludes comic Arthur Douglas / cosmic-powered versions.
characters.summary: Alien warrior and Guardian who fights as a brutal melee combatant. Sources show him overpowering several guards and killing a Kree-allied opponent in the films; no comic cosmic powers are claimed here.

mechanisms: high physical toughness shown in fights (not quantified)

weaknesses: Literal-minded and reckless; one fan wiki notes he lost when he drunkenly challenged Ronin's forces
Was turned to dust by Thanos' snap (MCU)
Cannot swim (fan-wiki list, unconfirmed for film)

feats.claim: Overpowered multiple Kyln guards and Sakaaran warriors with little effort.
feats.citation: Guardians of the Galaxy series wiki, Drax page

unknowns: No sourced strength or durability figure for the MCU version.
Fan-wiki bullets mix comic and MCU feats; only the MCU-tagged ones were considered.

sources.supports: Expert combatant able to overpower multiple opponents including Kyln guards and Sakaaran warriors
Fan wiki list marks MCU feats: kills Korath, tears apart drones, snapped by Thanos; comic feats listed separately
MCU Drax: Dave Bautista; family killed by Ronin working for Thanos; appears in Guardians, Infinity War, Endgame

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Druig (Barry Keoghan) in Eternals (2021). Excludes comic Earth-616 Druig.
characters.summary: Eternal whose power is mind control over large groups of humans, used to hold a Peruvian community for centuries. He can also contribute to the Eternals' Uni-Mind.

techniques: mind control of many people at once
controlling deviants (after a Kappa deviant copied the power)
offense.range: line of sight to crowd scale (sources say an entire city)

mechanisms: Eternal resistance to damage and disease (Looper, general to Eternals)

conditional.dependsOn: Uni-Mind combined power of the other Eternals

weaknesses: Mind control is not shown to stop a Deviant that had already copied it
Needs the Eternals' combined power for Celestial-scale targets

feats.claim: Controlled an entire community of humans for about 500 years.

unknowns: No limit on number or range of targets is sourced.
Physical combat ability is not detailed in the cited pages.

sources.supports: Mind control used to run a community in Peruvian Amazonia; controlled many deviants after Kappa; planned to halt the Emergence
Druig displays nearly unlimited control over humans; with the Uni-Mind he controls Tiamut
Can control and command an entire city of people with ease
Eternals resistant to damage and disease, can fuse into a Uni-Mind (general Eternal info)

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Maya Lopez / Echo (Alaqua Cox) in Hawkeye (2021) and Echo (2024). Excludes comic photographic-reflexes version.
characters.summary: Deaf, prosthetic-leg martial artist trained in several fighting styles. In her series she gains inherited Choctaw abilities (enhanced strength, speed and durability) from her ancestors.

techniques: martial arts (capoeira, boxing, taekwondo, judo, MMA per GamesRadar)
sharpshooting (as teased in Hawkeye, per ComingSoon via Yahoo)
ancestral powers marked by face tattoos

mechanisms: enhanced durability from ancestral powers (pre-release report)

conditional.dependsOn: Accepting her heritage; manifested during the Echo series

weaknesses: Pre-series Maya is a human fighter without powers
Does not have the comic copycat ability; the director called it lame
unknowns: Pre-release article lists powers; the finished series may differ in scope.

sources.supports: MCU Maya is an extremely skilled martial artist trained in capoeira, boxing, taekwondo, judo and MMA
Reported powers from Choctaw ancestors: enhanced strength, speed, durability, sharpshooting; face tattoo when she uses them
Wikipedia mirror: MCU Maya lacks the comic ability; Choctaw heritage is the source of her powers; not Ronin
In the show her fighting skill comes from experience rather than a power

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Ego (Kurt Russell) in Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2. Excludes comic Ego the Living Planet.
characters.summary: Celestial who built a planet around his energy core and wears a human avatar. He reshapes matter on his planet and was defeated when the Guardians destroyed his brain.

techniques: creating a human body to inhabit (Comic Vine)

conditional.dependsOn: Planting seedlings across planets; his own power is bounded until then (not detailed in the pages)

weaknesses: Needs Peter Quill's Celestial power for his plan
unknowns: No sourced strength or energy figure.
Power set partly inferred from comic sources in some pages.

sources.supports: MCU Ego is a core of pure energy that built a planet around himself, unlike the biological comic version
MCU: ancient Celestial, father of Peter Quill, can create a human body to inhabit
Guardians could defeat Ego because Star-Lord had Celestial powers and they knew to hit his brain
Powers work like assimilation for matter not part of his body; plan to destroy the universe with Peter's powers

characters.continuity: Max Dillon (Jamie Foxx) from The Amazing Spider-Man 2, as pulled into the MCU in Spider-Man: No Way Home. Excludes comic Earth-616 Electro.
characters.summary: Former Oscorp engineer who became a living electrical capacitor. In No Way Home he gains enhanced power from the arc reactor and fights all three Spider-Men at once.

mechanisms: power levels boosted by absorbed energy

conditional.dependsOn: Arc reactor energy taken in No Way Home

weaknesses: Short-circuited by water when fully charged (fandom page)
Gwen's override overload destroyed him in his own universe
Can be cured and stripped of powers

feats.claim: Battled all three Spider-Men at once with enhanced powers.

unknowns: No sourced voltage or output figure for the film version.
Power level after the arc reactor is not quantified.

sources.supports: Living capacitor; took arc reactor in No Way Home; fought three Spider-Men at once; exploded in ASM2 via Gwen's override
Powers: electrostatic energy, lightning bolts, electrical detection, recharging; vulnerable to water when fully charged
MCU version later stabilised with a device allowing a human appearance

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Netflix Elektra Natchios (Élodie Yung) in Daredevil season 2 and The Defenders. Excludes the 2003/2005 films and comic version.
characters.summary: Hand-trained assassin and Black Sky, with superhuman strength, speed and toughness and slowed ageing. She fights with twin sai.
weaknesses: Dependent on Hand resurrection for her enhanced state
Comic psychic powers are not present in this version
unknowns: Black Sky abilities beyond stated physical traits not detailed here.

sources.supports: MCU Elektra is a Black Sky with super-strength, toughness, speed and slow ageing, unlike the comic psychic powers
Played by Élodie Yung; expert martial artist using a pair of sais
Netflix Daredevil and The Defenders origin streamlined and rooted in mysticism

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe Sam Wilson as Falcon (Anthony Mackie) with the EXO-7 Falcon suit. Excludes comic avian telepathy.
characters.summary: Non-powered former pararescueman whose flight and offense come from the EXO-7 wing suit and a Redwing drone. No innate superpowers.

techniques: EXO-7 jet-pack wings with retractable flight

mobility: Powered flight via the wing suit
weaknesses: No superpowers; abilities depend on the suit
Redwing is a drone, not a living bird
unknowns: Later Captain America suit upgrades not covered.

sources.supports: MCU Sam is a hero forged by training and technology, not superpowers
No inherent powers in the MCU; Redwing is a Stark-tech drone
Abilities concentrated in a jet pack with retractable wings for nimble flight
